channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Brazil's Lula, 80, says he is 'in great shape' as he launches fourth term bid
item.description: Brazil's Workers' Party on Sunday formally endorsed President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for what is expected to be his final reelection bid, setting up an October election increasingly shaped by concerns over foreign influence and an unusually internationalized campaign.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Wiebes wins second consecutive Tour de France Femmes stage
item.description: Lorena Wiebes underlined her dominance at the Tour de France Femmes on Sunday, powering to a second straight sprint victory in Geneva to tighten her grip on the race leader's yellow jersey.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: At least 14 dead as Ukraine and Russia exchange strikes
item.description: Ukrainian attacks killed at least nine people across Russia on Sunday, while Russian strikes left at least five dead in Ukraine, officials said. Both sides intensified long-range attacks despite stalled efforts to negotiate an end to the war.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Fire spread deeper into Athens region
item.description:
Two firefighting helicopters have collided while battling a wildfire west of Athens in Greece. The Greek fire service says each helicopter was carrying a two-person crew, and a search-and-rescue operation is now underway.
Greece is battling wildfires on multiple fronts, with the Prime Minister warning of “extremely difficult” days ahead. Dozens of homes have been damaged or destroyed, and three firefighters have died this week. Catherine Viette has more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: US, Israel to hold off on Iran strikes
item.description: US President Donald Trump has pulled back from plans for major new strikes on Iran, in his latest climbdown after weeks of threatening to hit Tehran hard. The president said late Saturday that the US would hold off, provided a deal can be reached quickly. It follows a phone call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who reportedly urged de-escalation, amid fears that Iran could retaliate against the Kingdom and other Gulf states. In announcing that he was calling off the strikes, Trump said Israel had “joined him in this commitment”. But Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has yet to comment. Matthew-Mary Caruchet, from France 24 international affair desk, shares further insights.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France steps up fire prevention
item.description: As France grapples with its worst wildfire season in decades, officials are looking for ways to stop fires before they even start. Catherine Viette has more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Gironde megafire contained: Nearly 3,000 firefighters remain deployed
item.description: Meanwhile, France’s vast wildfire near Bordeaux remains contained. Most of the 200,000 people who were told to evacuate have now returned home, although parts of the fire are still burning. The blaze has scorched an area four times the size of Paris. James Andre has the latest.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Spain's Ceuta navigates aftermath of border surge as most migrants return home
item.description: Ceuta was returning to normal over the weekend after an unprecedented migrant surge that saw up to 60,000 people enter the tiny Spanish exclave from Morocco in just two days. But with at least 72 migrants dead and most arrivals having already returned to Morocco, residents were still grappling with the humanitarian, political and social fallout.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: The week in pictures: European wildfires, a woolly mammoth and a migrant influx at Spain's Ceuta
item.description: Fires burned across much of Europe, an earthquake in Japan killed dozens, record-low water levels in Bulgaria exposed the remains of a woolly mammoth, and tens of thousands sought to cross into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta before eventually returning home: FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Capital One bank cites money-laundering probe to justify closing Trump Organization accounts
item.description: Capital One Financial on Friday defended its decision to close more than 300 Trump-affiliated bank accounts back in 2021, stating that it did so after a money-laundering review. The ‌disclosure marks the first time a bank has formally tied money-laundering concerns to US President Donald Trump's family business.
item.source: © John Moore, Getty Images via AFP
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Two killed after firefighting helicopters in Greece collide
item.description: Two Greek firefighting helicopters collided in midair on Sunday as they were fighting a wind-driven wildfire west of Athens, sending one aircraft plummeting to the ground. Two crew members, a Greek and a Danish national, perished in the crash.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Hungary: Successive heatwaves drain Danube river used to cool nuclear plant
item.description: Prolonged drought and extreme heat across Europe have also triggered an energy crisis. For the first time ever, Hungary announced the shutdown of the country’s only nuclear power plant, after water levels in the Danube fell to a record low. Peter O’Brien explains.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Football: Brentford sign Ligue 1 star Mamadou Sangaré for €48 million
item.description: Mali's international Mamadou Sangaré is heading to the Premier League following a stellar season with french club Lens. He has officially joined Brentford in a landmark €48 million transfer, setting a new record sale for the French club.
item.dc:creator: L'Equipe TV

item.title: Colombia police station bombed wounding 14 people
item.description: Colombia’s government has blamed rebel groups for a truck bomb that wounded 14 people near the border with Venezuela. The attack came less than a week before President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella is due to take office. He has said he plans to end the current administration’s peace negotiations with various armed groups. Morgan Ayre reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Peru: Tourist plane crashes killing all 13 people aboard
item.description: Eleven foreign tourists and two crew members have been killed after a small sightseeing plane crashed shortly after take-off in Peru. The cause of the crash is not yet known, and an investigation is underway. Peter O' Brien has more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France: Most of 224,000 evacuees allowed to return home after devastating fires
item.description: Here in France, a wildfire in the mountainous southeastern Var department, which had been brought under control three days ago, flared up again on Friday, forcing authorities to evacuate nearly 2,500 people overnight. Meanwhile, our reporter James Andre visited Gironde, where France’s biggest wildfire in more than 70 years was recently brought under control.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Gaza: overnight Israeli strikes kill at least 8
item.description: Israel carried out overnight strikes in Gaza, killing at least eight people. This is a look at the Strip this Sunday morning. In one attack, an Israeli military helicopter struck an apartment, killing a husband and wife. In another, an elderly man and a child were killed. Earlier on Saturday, at least seven people were killed in strikes that also damaged medical supplies at a hospital. The attacks came after Hamas said it had agreed to the latest stage of a deal aimed at ending the war. Morgan Ayre reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Three people killed in Moscow bombing
item.description: A blast near the centre of Moscow has killed at least three people and injured 21 others. It happened at around 8pm local time, when a homemade explosive device detonated as a woman tried to enter a restaurant and was stopped by a security guard, according to Russia’s National Anti-Terrorist Committee. Both the woman and the security guard were killed, along with a visitor at the restaurant, which was hosting a private function. Authorities have not said who they believe was the target, but Russian independent media report it may have been a military official. The attack is also suspected of being linked to the war in Ukraine. In recent years, several senior Russian military figures have been assassinated in and around Moscow, with the Kremlin blaming Kyiv for those attacks. Morgan Ayre has this story.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: At least three killed in 'terrorist' bombing of Moscow restaurant, Russian officials say
item.description: At least three people have been killed and 21 wounded after a homemade explosive device was detonated at a restaurant in Moscow, Russian officials said late Saturday. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin called the attack a “brutal terrorist act” but did not say who he thought was responsible.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Trump holds off on striking Iran, calls for 'rapid' deal to end the conflict
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Saturday that the United States and Israel had agreed to hold off on new strikes on Iran – provided a deal to end the months-long conflict is "rapidly" reached. Iran's acting defence minister said his country would "neither ‌be caught off ​guard nor remain passive" in the face of new US threats. Read our live blog to see how events unfolded.
item.source: © Majid Asgaripour, West Asia News Agency via Reuters
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Spain installs floating barrier in Ceuta after migration influx
item.description: Spanish authorities said Saturday they were installing a floating barrier on the sea border between its North African territory of Ceuta and neighbouring Morocco after a deadly surge of tens of thousands of migrants into the territory earlier in the week prompted alarm across the European Union.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Israeli strikes on residential buildings kill at least 13 in Gaza
item.description: Israeli strikes on Gaza overnight killed at least 13 people after hitting several residential buildings, local authorities said on Sunday. Seven people were also killed in Israeli strikes on Saturday, a day after Hamas said it had agreed to the latest deal on ending the war.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24
